# <span id="aanchor134"></span> Sample Analysis Editor

The Sample Analysis Editor contains a detailed layout for hydrocarbon and non-hydrocarbon analysis samples. The Sample Analysis Editor includes a Mole %, Mass %, and LV % component breakdown for hydrocarbon sources, and a NHC Mole %, NHC Mass %, and NHC LV % component breakdown for non-hydrocarbon sources.

For hydrocarbon samples, users can enter Mole %, Mass %, or LV % values, and FLOWCAL will then calculate other properties, such as densities in different units (top right), component Mole %, Mass %, and/or LV %. All calculations are performed based on the Characteristics. Calculations will not occur for non-hydrocarbon sample analysis.

Users can also set a hydrocarbon or non-hydrocarbon liquids product designation for the sample, which is used during LQ apply operations to ensure that like products are applied between the product in the sample and the product in the meter data or batch. FLOWCAL will not perform a sample apply for disparate products. Options on the sample analysis editor will vary depending on the product fluid service (hydrocarbon or non-hydrocarbon). The Sample Analysis Editor grid will not change if you are viewing a non-hydrocarbon sample.

<div class="procedure">

To enter a new sample source analysis:

1.  Go to **Open** \> **Sample Analysis**.
2.  Click the **New Detail** button at the bottom of the **Sample Quality Editor**.
3.  Click **Edit**.
4.  Enter the sample date.
5.  Enter the <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">Sample ID<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>The Sample ID is unique across all standalone samples in a FLOWCAL database. This is in contrast to liquid quality source samples, whose unique identification is the LQ number and sample date. The Sample ID can contain up to 25 characters and is required for all standalone samples.</span></a>.
6.  Enter the Quality information.
7.  Click **Save**.

## Screen Details

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Override">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Override Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Override">

- **HC Property Override** - Allows users to select a given set of GPA TP-17 hydrocarbon properties to be used in calculations, including user-defined sets.

- **Base Density Calc Method** - Allows users to override the default density calculation based on HC properties and GPA-2145 constants. Options are COSTALD, Modified TP-2, and REFPROP.

  This field is disabled for non-hydrocarbon sample analyses.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Base Density Calc Method">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Base Density Calc Method (Hydrocarbon Samples Only)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Base Density Calc Method">

Base Density Calc Method allows the user to override the default density calculation based on HC Properties and GPA-2145 constants. Options are COSTALD, Modified TP-2, and REFPROP. If a Product using Table-E (TP-27) or Table E Extended (TP-27 EXT) table is designated on the sample, the Base Density Calc Method will automatically be populated with the Default Base Density Calculation set on the Product. The user will still have the ability to manually select a Base Density Calc Method to be used for the sample density calculation.

| Sample Density Calc Method Defined for Product? | Base Density Calc Method Defined? | Base Density Calculation Method Used |
|:--:|:--:|----|
| Y | N | Product default source base density calc |
| Y | Y | Text file or manual entry record base density calc method |
| N | Y | Text file or manual entry record base density calc method |
| N | N | Default to current behavior - Use HC Properties |

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="C6 Plus">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />C6+ Extended (Hydrocarbon Samples Only)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="C6 Plus">

To access C6+ Extended:

1.  Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis**.
2.  Select **Gas Quality**.
3.  Select **Source Analysis**.
4.  Click **New Detail**.
5.  Enter **To** and **From** dates.
6.  Click the **C6+ Extended** button.

The user may also specify the C6+ Component Breakdown for a given sample by clicking on the button. This feature allows the user to account for the presence of C7 through C*(n)* in a given sample that has mole percent components up to C6. To allow FLOWCAL to calculate an accurate density and molecular weight for the sample, the minimum data point set to populate is the Molar Mass and Absolute Density of the C6+ components.

The default set of Extended Characteristics assumes that the C6 composition provided is only C6. A C6+ split can be defined for standalone samples by going to the System Factors Editor (Admin **→** System Options → System Factors) and specifying a split there.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 305;height: 375;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Considerations">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Source Apply Considerations</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Considerations">

For the Source Apply process, the meter or location and source must have the same unit set (US or SI). A "Unit Set Discrepancy" exception is generated if both the meter or location and the source are not in the same unit set. This exception is also generated if the temperature base and pressure base of the meter or location are not in the same unit set.

FLOWCAL does not apply the purity sample from the product to any records where an LQ Assignment is set for the meter or location during the time frame of that record. This allows users to use the sample product in FLOWCAL as a purity and a non-purity product on a per meter or location basis.

For example: Meter 1 will use Propane as a purity, so Meter 1 will not have a Quality Source assigned. The purity sample will automatically apply onto the records for that meter. Meter 2 will be used as a non-purity propane meter, so Meter 2 will have a LQ Source Assignment setup. The purity sample will not apply to any records during the duration of the assignment. A sample must be applied through either the Source Assignment, or a Sample Override

If a density value is not found as per the Apply Density option, FLOWCAL uses the next available density. In other words, the process fails over to using a sample density value in the order depicted in the table below. An exception is generated if a density value is used that is not the first Apply Density choice. If no density value is found even after the fail over process, then another exception is generated alerting the user about the lack of a density value.

| Apply Density Option | First Failover   | Second Failover  |
|----------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Relative Density     | API Gravity      | Absolute Density |
| API Gravity          | Relative Density | Absolute Density |
| Absolute Density     | Relative Density | API Gravity      |

Applying a source/sample performs as follows when applying density to tickets:

- **For Observed Temperature:**
  - If the user chooses to apply density and the ticket it set to Absolute Density, the Observed Temperature is set to the Base Temperature of the Sample.
  - If the user chooses not to apply a density at all, the Observed Temperature is not modified.
- **For Observed Pressure:**
  - If the user chooses to apply density and the ticket is set to Gauge Density, the Observed Pressure is set to 0.0.
  - If the user chooses to apply density and the ticket it set to Absolute Density, the Observed Pressure is set to the Base Pressure of the Sample.
  - If the user chooses not to apply a density at all, the Observed Pressure is not modified.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Apply Extended">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />C+ Type “Apply Extended As” Rules</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Apply Extended">

Standalone samples do not currently support anything other than C6+, so C6+ extended characteristics will always be applied with a standalone sample. Standalone samples also do not currently support having a full analysis, so the sample will always be applied as-is.

In the Quality Source Analysis Editor, if the “Has Extended Analysis” option is selected, FLOWCAL will follow the "Apply Extended As" value defined under **Volume Editor** \> **Characteristic** \> **Batch Sample Override**.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Extended As Ex">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

<div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Extended As Ex">

If a sample contains a full analysis (220 components) that goes out to C10, and the “Apply Extended As” option in any of the three places listed above is set to C6+, FLOWCAL will sum the values from C6 to C10 and apply the sum to C6. FLOWCAL will also apply the C6+ extended characteristics.

</div>

</div>

If the “Has Extended Analysis” option is not selected, FLOWCAL will apply the sample as it is given on the source and will apply the extended characteristics for the highest component that has a value. If the highest component that has a value is less that C6, the C6+ extended characteristics will be applied.

</div>
